source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: FY25 was a transformational year for Lupin Manufacturing Solutions (LMS)... to emerge as a differentiated CDMO partner. Through API Plus and LMS, Lupin is ensuring secure global supply chains and elevating India's stature in the global API and CDMO landscape — aligns with supply-chain diversification/CDMO outsourcing trend, but no explicit China+1 phrase with quantified revenue attribution found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt ~INR 103 crore as of Q3 FY25 (very low leverage); no floating-rate liability percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: North America accounted for 38% of Lupin's global sales in FY25 (US sales USD 925mn vs USD 815mn FY24); India formulations 34%; Other Developed Markets 11%.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin named among Group A (11 selected applicants) under India's Rs 15,000 crore PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals.

Divi's has pursued diversified raw-material sourcing to reduce China dependence; custom synthesis and peptides described as growth engines; reportedly Category 2 API/KSM PLI applicant with capacity expansions 'where Chinese pricing had previously made domestic investment unviable.' No explicit China+1 framing directly tied to revenue growth located.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Historically minimal to no debt; no floating-rate liability disclosure found.

crude_exposure.evidence: API/custom-synthesis manufacturing relies on petroleum-based solvents; solvent recovery systems cited to lower input costs, but no specific raw-material cost percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were 90% of FY25 sales, US+Europe combined 74% of export revenue.

pli_scheme.evidence: Part of Category 2 API-and-KSM applicant pool under India's PLI scheme, projects targeting fermentation-based APIs at Bollaram and Vishakhapatnam.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 narrative found. Sun Pharma operates API manufacturing across India, Hungary, US, Australia, Israel; API ~4% of FY25 revenue (Rs 2,129.2 crore, +11.0% YoY), not framed as China+1.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25: India formulations Rs 169,230mn (~31% of Rs 54,543.5cr total); US formulations USD 1,921mn (+3.6%); Emerging Markets USD 1,114mn (+7.0%); RoW USD 847mn (+4.5%); Global Specialty USD 1,216mn (+17.1%).

pli_scheme.evidence: Listed among 55 companies selected for India's Rs 15,000 crore pharma PLI scheme, reportedly Category 1/Group A; plants in Halol, Gujarat and Dadra relevant to scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Alkem participates in export markets across ~40 countries, 'seeking to reduce reliance on any single geography.' Owns US-based API manufacturing (Azusa, California) supporting supply chain control. No explicit China+1 framing with quantified revenue attribution found.

rural.evidence: Alkem recognized for strong branded-generics distribution in rural/semi-urban and tier 2-3 India (domestic business grew 6.5% YoY to Rs 8,983.7cr FY25), but no specific rural revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25: India sales Rs 8,983.7cr (+6.5%, ~69% of total); International sales Rs 3,821cr (-4.5%, ~29-30% of total), total revenue ~Rs 12,964.5-13,458.3cr.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not found among the 55 companies publicly identified as PLI scheme beneficiaries.

china_plus_one.evidence: MD & Group CEO letter: 'Sona Comstar is emerging as a strategic partner of choice in a reshaped global supply chain' amid 'protectionist policies and tariff-related uncertainties'; Chairman Emeritus letter: 'we are leveraging [trade shifts] as opportunities to strengthen our position...we are well-placed to benefit from the shifts in the new trade policies.' Manufacturing footprint spans India, China, Mexico, and USA ('China, Mexico, and the USA are key final assembly and localisation nodes'). Strategy described as 'diversifying across products, customers, and geographies' and 'reducing concentration risks.' rate_sensitive.evidence: INR 26.7 billion net cash at year-end FY25 per MD's letter; low-leverage profile, no floating-rate liability percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: MD's letter (Vivek Vikram Singh): 'more than 70% of our revenue comes from markets outside India,' with North America cited as a key market where Sona is 'among the largest suppliers of BEV differential assemblies, differential bevel gears, and starter motors.'

pli_scheme.evidence: CFO's Review (direct AR quote): 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.'

china_plus_one.evidence: Company's CDMO business grew strongly (~27% of international business FY24, +18% YoY Q4 FY25) amid industry commentary that Indian CDMOs benefit from global pharma China+1 diversification and proposed US BIOSECURE Act. No direct AR quote explicitly framing this as 'China+1' confirmed (primary AR PDF inaccessible, 403); inferred from earnings coverage and industry analysis of JB Pharma's CDMO growth.

pli_scheme.evidence: No public disclosure linking J B Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals to Government of India PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI (bulk drugs/API) relevance tied to former subsidiary Glenmark Life Sciences (divested to Nirma 2023, no longer consolidated); no direct PLI beneficiary status found for parent entity FY2024-25.

china_plus_one.evidence: Cemindia Projects (formerly ITD Cementation India Ltd) is a domestic infrastructure EPC contractor, not an export-oriented manufacturer; no China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative found.

govt_capex.evidence: Pure-play Engineering & Construction (EPC) contractor for large infrastructure: Mass Rapid Transit Systems/metro (Kolkata, Pune, Delhi), highways/bridges (Bihar road-cum-elevated corridor), maritime/ports (JSW port), airports, hydro/dams/tunnels/irrigation, industrial structures — sectors dominated by government and PSU clients. As of March 2024, order book mix (third-party concall summary): Government 49% + PSU 18% + Private 33% (~67% public-sector), though this is order-book composition not audited revenue split; no FY2025-26-specific breakdown found. FY26 order book record Rs 24,545 crore (~2.4x annual revenue); data centers (~Rs 3,000cr) emerging as new private-sector growth segment.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt-to-equity 0.22 for FY2025-26 (low leverage); credit rating upgrades to A+ (Stable) from CARE and ICRA during the year; no disclosed floating vs fixed-rate borrowing split found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary cost inputs are steel, cement, aggregates and fuel/bitumen (indirect crude-oil linkage via diesel and bitumen), but no disclosed raw-material cost percentage found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Operations described as 'mainly in India' within a single Engineering & Construction segment, with limited overseas exposure (e.g. a project in Abu Dhabi); no USD/foreign-currency revenue percentage or hedging policy disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable — PLI schemes target manufacturing sectors; Cemindia Projects is an infrastructure EPC/construction contractor with no indication of PLI participation.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company hedges trade receivables in major currencies (USD, AUD, EUR, JPY, GBP) via forward contracts to minimize volatility in realized exchange gain/loss; derivatives not designated as hedge accounting relationships, marked to fair value through P&L.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'A substantial portion of the Company's revenue is generated in foreign currencies, while majority of expenses are incurred in Indian Rupees.' 'The Company hedges the trade receivables in major currencies with the objective to minimize the volatility in realized exchange gain or loss.' Outstanding forward contracts as at March 31, 2024: Sell USD 88.60mn, AUD 11.22mn, EUR 14.60mn, JPY 505.00mn, GBP 3.40mn. Net unhedged FX exposure INR 2,630.44mn (FY23: INR 1,332.90mn).

china_plus_one.evidence: Company cites export-led model with sales in 100+ countries; Flat Products unit selected under India's PLI scheme for specialty steel (high-strength automotive steel, CRGO electrical steel) framed as a 'substantial opportunity for import substitution.' No explicit China+1 framing found, but import-substitution/export-diversification narrative present.

rural.evidence: Company markets TMT bars/long products as central to India's construction and urbanisation growth; third-party pricing data shows TMT bar prices in smaller towns/rural districts of West Bengal running lower due to lower demand intensity, but no rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Long products segment (billets, sponge iron, TMT bars, structural steel) positioned around construction/infrastructure demand; secondary commentary links India's national infrastructure pipeline to sustained steel demand, but no explicit % of revenue tied to government capex disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore, iron ore fines, manganese ore, chrome ore and coal (domestically sourced); no crude-oil or petroleum-linked input exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Management referenced target to roughly double export revenue from ~US$150mn toward ~US$300mn (implying exports ~8-10% of FY25 consolidated revenue), but no explicit USD-revenue % or hedging policy disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Shyam Metalics Flat Products selected as qualifier under India's PLI scheme for specialty steel, targeting high-strength automotive steel and CRGO electrical steel, described as significant import-substitution opportunity; no revenue % attributable to PLI disclosed.

ABB.report_year: CY2023 (FY Jan-Dec 2023, ABB India's calendar-year fiscal convention)

china_plus_one.evidence: Chairman's letter: 'the robotics solutions are also playing a significant role in the nation's rapid strides in self reliance and localization of value chain in the electronics segment.' Also: 'India's move to specialized high end manufacturing was further catalyzed by ABB's robotics solutions in electronics, painting and cleaning of electric vehicles...' MD&A theme of 'Making in India for India and the world' with continuous focus on localization. No explicit use of phrase 'China+1'.

govt_capex.evidence: MD&A: 'a year characterized by resurgence in capital expenditure, driven by government initiatives to pursue one of the world's largest infrastructure expansion programs.' Outlook: 'ABB India is strategically positioned to expand its market presence, capitalizing on the upsurge in economic activities across various sectors including power transmission, clean energy, railways, metro, and public infrastructure. Government investments provide further support to these endeavors.' Chairman's letter cites contributions to roads, railways, modern ports/airports, semi-high-speed rail/metro electrification (Bhopal, Indore metros).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Key Financial Ratios note: 'Debt Equity Ratio - Not Applicable, as the Company did not have any borrowings in the current and previous year' (Dec 2023 and Dec 2022). Net cash position of ~INR 4,727 crore as of Dec 31, 2023.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw materials/components consumed INR 5,512.48cr (~53% of INR 10,446.52cr revenue), but composition is electrical/electronic components, copper, steel; Note 39 commodity-risk lists only copper and silver futures hedged — no crude oil or oil-derivative exposure disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: The Company continued to conservatively hedge at the point of commitment or at balance sheet levels for protecting contract margins.
inr_exposure.evidence: Note 39(ii) Foreign Currency Risk: 'The Company operates internationally and is exposed to foreign exchange risk arising from foreign currency transactions, primarily with respect to the CHF, USD, SEK and EUR.' Outstanding forward contracts Dec 31, 2023: exports INR 315.90cr total (USD portion INR 256.69cr), imports INR 708.46cr total (USD portion INR 193.04cr).

pli_scheme.evidence: Outlook: 'The focus on local manufacturing with Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme in digital India and digital infrastructure...are all drivers which augur well for ABB India's growth.' Motion segment outlook: 'the focus on domestic manufacturing with PLI will further growth opportunities.' PLI discussed as a macro/customer-side demand driver, not as a scheme ABB India itself directly receives incentives under.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No specific floating-rate debt % disclosed; generally low-leverage company (AR PDF fetch failed).
